description: Live view of what the market-data collectors are writing into the shared `dropset` database: candles, cross-source agreement, throughput, freshness, and coverage. Read top-down — the freshness tiles answer 'is ingestion alive right now', everything below answers 'and is it any good'.

panels.description: Wall-clock seconds since each feed last committed a batch, straight off `feed_cursors.updated_at`. This is the only true wall-clock liveness signal in the schema — every other panel measures candle-bucket time, which a backfill can advance without the feed being currently healthy. A wall of green is the end-to-end proof that a feeds change works.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  feed,
  extract(epoch FROM now() - updated_at) AS age_secs
FROM feed_cursors
ORDER BY feed

panels.title: Feed cursor age (wall clock)

panels.description: Seconds since the newest candle bucket each source/product has on record. The floor is one granularity by construction — the collector persists only closed buckets, so a perfectly healthy 60s feed reads 60-120s and never 0. The thresholds are set above that floor accordingly; treat this as 'how stale is the data I would quote from', and the cursor-age tile beside it as 'is the process alive'.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  source || ' ' || product_id AS feed,
  extract(epoch FROM now()) - max(bucket_start) AS age_secs
FROM cex_prices
WHERE source IN (${source:sqlstring})
  AND product_id IN (${product_id:sqlstring})
  AND granularity_secs = $granularity
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Last candle age

panels.description: OHLC candles as recorded, one panel per selected product. This is the 'real chart' view and the screenshot artifact. It reads a single source ($candle_source) on purpose: candles from two venues share a bucket key but are different series, so overlaying them would interleave bars rather than compare them. Use the overlay panel below to compare sources.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS "time",
  "open",
  "high",
  "low",
  "close",
  "volume"
FROM cex_prices
WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
  AND source = '$candle_source'
  AND product_id = '$product_id'
  AND granularity_secs = $granularity
ORDER BY bucket_start

panels.title: OHLC $product_id ($candle_source, ${granularity}s buckets)

panels.description: Every selected source's closing print for every selected product, overlaid on one axis. Relative-value divergence is visible as separating lines: two venues quoting the same pair should track within basis, and a mispriced or mis-mapped source shows up on sight as a line at the wrong level. With one collector running this is a single series — it populates as sources land, with no dashboard edit.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS "time",
  source || ' ' || product_id AS metric,
  "close" AS value
FROM cex_prices
WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
  AND source IN (${source:sqlstring})
  AND product_id IN (${product_id:sqlstring})
  AND granularity_secs = $granularity
ORDER BY bucket_start

panels.title: Price by source

panels.description: Rows landed per minute, per source. Note the axis is candle-bucket time, not insert time: the schema records no insert timestamp, so this counts buckets by the minute they cover. For a live 60s feed that is a flat line at one row per product per minute, and a collector that dies mid-window drops visibly to zero. A collector dead for the whole window contributes no series at all rather than a zero line - that case is what the freshness tiles above are for. The bucket is a fixed one minute rather than the dashboard interval, so the number means the same thing at every zoom level; the cost is that a multi-day range returns a point per minute.

targets.rawSql:
-- The CTE is load-bearing, not style. Grafana captures macro
-- arguments with a regex that stops at the first closing paren, so
-- wrapping the epoch column in a to_timestamp call inside the
-- time-group macro leaves it one truncated argument and the query
-- fails to interpolate. Converting the column in a CTE first hands
-- the macro a bare column name, which is all it can parse. For the
-- same reason, do not name a macro in a comment here: the scanner
-- does not skip comments and will try to interpolate the example.
WITH bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS bucket_ts,
    source
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source IN (${source:sqlstring})
    AND product_id IN (${product_id:sqlstring})
)
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(bucket_ts, '1m', 0),
  source AS metric,
  count(*) AS value
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Rows per minute by source

panels.description: Which source covers which product, over the last $coverage_mins minutes. This is the panel that answers 'do we want another collector here' - a product with one source has no cross-check, and a product with none is a gap. Deliberately NOT filtered by the source/product variables: its job is to show everything arriving, including series the current selection hides.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  source,
  product_id,
  granularity_secs,
  count(*) AS buckets,
  to_timestamp(max(bucket_start)) AS latest_bucket,
  (extract(epoch FROM now()) - max(bucket_start))::bigint AS age_secs
FROM cex_prices
WHERE bucket_start >= extract(epoch FROM now()) - ($coverage_mins * 60)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 1, 2, 3

panels.title: Source x product coverage (last $coverage_mins min)
